boundary: Bounded source decisions before C3 authoring and Worker scaffold revision. No registry expansion, task content, learner state, source execution or release changes.

ardan_search.claim: Only this finite template set was inspected; not an exhaustive claim about all external exercises. No template is selected as a task-content donor.

semantic_reference.usage: Fact checking only. No documentation example, task text/code/test or solution is admitted as task content.
facts: A full buffered send waits for buffer space; receive drains an existing pending element.
After buffered values are drained, receives from a closed channel return the element zero value with ok=false; a nil channel cannot proceed in select.
Go starts a new goroutine; no ambient launch-order or fairness guarantee is assumed.
Context derives parent cancellation and the earlier deadline; releasing a child does not cancel the parent.
Wait waits until every other goroutine in the current bubble is durably blocked; fake time advances only when every goroutine in that bubble is durably blocked.

decisions.reason: The bounded first-party goroutine template asks for two counting goroutines plus WaitGroup and printed output; it has no isolated supplied runner/handle boundary. Author the supplied-handle launch exercise independently to introduce go without requiring the learner to design channel synchronization or join internals.

No already admitted artifact isolates receive-before-send on an open full capacity-one channel. Existing ClosedReceive and OwnedValues cover different closed-channel contracts. The reviewed channel templates combine ping-pong, random fan-out, aggregation or worker shutdown; author a distinct bounded single-slot replacement contract.

Retain the ready Worker task ID, Start API, eight required mutants, role and assessed skills. Existing original creation/project/source identity is preserved. Add only the reviewed failure-safe gated helper and blocked/released/completed example; independent-call and premature-completion cases remain learner-owned. Exact old-workspace compatibility tooling must precede the authored starter/hints change.

None of the four bounded channel templates merges exactly two caller-supplied finite streams while preserving per-stream occurrence order and disabling closed inputs. Random fan-out aggregation and worker shutdown are broader different contracts. Author the finite MergeTwo task independently; no SHAD or reference-only concurrency task is a donor.

The closest bounded channel template uses random workers and a separate shutdown channel, not a supplied context-aware forwarding stage with cancellation at both receive and backpressured send. Existing CancelWorker checks derivation/cancellation, not forwarding ownership. Author an independent narrow stage with explicit termination and caller-input ownership; no broad worker-pool adaptation.

Current duration and PropagateContext tasks do not assess child timeout ownership, earlier parent deadline or cancel-on-return. The bounded template set has no timeout wrapper. Author independently using pinned context/synctest semantic facts only, without adapting documentation examples or tests.

conditions: Independent source approval before content authoring; source approval is not promotion or executable acceptance.
Five originals require ADR 0008 identity, real creation record, actual content digest, empty external task sources and deferred release binding.
Worker exact compatibility tooling precedes content revision; preserve Start API, old histories/workspace bytes and all eight mandatory variants.
C3 is six changes: five new tasks and one existing scaffold revision. P13 has no new task ID/address.
Concurrency checks require race and controlled failure-safe cleanup: no timeout-only mutant kills, uncontrolled clocks, sleep or random scheduling oracle.
No template, answer, external test/solution or documentation example is copied or closely paraphrased.

independent_review.scope: Source facts and bounded original-authoring/Worker-revision reasons only. Content, exact compatibility, promotion and executable acceptance require separate review.
